claim: Let \(\nu^k\) be uniform on \(\{-k+1,-k+3,\ldots,k-1\}\), and let \(T(\alpha)\) be the extremal mixture defined in Juškevičius (2024, Conjecture 6.1). For three independent summands with parameters \((\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3)=(1/20,1/20,1/10)\), the variance-matched common parameter is \(\alpha=619/10710\), but \(\mathcal Q_2(\sum_{i=1}^3T(\alpha_i))=7/160>219116707/5055477000=\mathcal Q_2(\sum_{i=1}^3T(\alpha))\); hence the conjectured variance-matched equalization inequality is false.

correctness.rationale: Exact finite-support derivation: the heterogeneous total variance is \(299\); \(\alpha_*=619/10710\) gives variance \(299/3\) per equalized summand; exact polynomial coefficients give \(\mathcal Q_2=7/160\) and \(\mathcal Q_2=219116707/5055477000\), whose strict difference is \(8241647/20221908000>0\). The included Fraction-based script exhaustively checks the finite convolutions.

evidence: Juškevičius §6 describes the known Kanter equalization result for \(\alpha_i\ge1/2\) and identifies the unrestricted statement as a conjecture.
Mattner–Roos, arXiv:math/0603522, §§1–2 treats a related two-point concentration bound for symmetric three-point convolutions.
Leader–Radcliffe's accessible abstract describes the special reciprocal-integer concentration-bound setting; its PDF retrieval timed out and its full text was not used.

Juškevičius–Kurauskas, arXiv:1912.08770v2, Theorem 1 and §3 give a sharp maximum-atom bound under a common individual atom cap; this does not compare the two different variance-matched sums in the present claim.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The present parameters are all below \(1/2\), and \(T(1/20)\), \(T(1/10)\) are uniform laws on 20- and 10-point progressions. The cited restricted equalization result does not cover this comparison. The related Juškevičius–Kurauskas theorem controls maximum atoms under a common cap, not the variance-matched ordering here. No inspected source states or implies the claimed variance-matched inequality for these parameters.
